evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'Your photo, stitched square by square.' plus the lede ('turns a photo into a cross-stitch chart in real thread colours, then hands you the squares') says what it is and for whom; the next step is muddied because 'Open the beta editor' actually scrolls to an on-page demo.
evidence.fit: Brief: the beta editor has no address yet. A keeps the label 'Open the beta editor' on 3 buttons (header, hero, final) and wires them via CONFIG.BETA_URL='' in app.js to scroll to #editor. The seller section ('We haven't set commercial terms yet') is a real path for sellers, but its CTA mails hello@crossling.app, an address the brief never supplied. The on-page photo import (file input, Width/Threads selects) matches 'turns a photo into a pattern'.
evidence.distinctiveness: The canvas draws real X-stitches on an aida-hole fabric texture, and the page uses a linen dot background and a serif display face. The structure is otherwise the stock kit: centred hero, a three-card 'How it works', a thread-swatch strip, a FAQ accordion and a final CTA band.
evidence.proof: Operated at 1440: brush, drag, fill, pick, unpick, undo, reset, the Stitches/Chart toggle, grid, the 11/14/16/18/28 fabric select (28 over 2 gives 4.4 cm, the same as 14-count, correct), the catalogue, swap (toast 'Swapped 827 for 353 Peach'), and 'Download chart as PNG' (crossling-sailboat.png with symbols and a key). Uploading a generated 200x150 PNG converted it locally to 40x30 with 12 threads. The editor heading sits at y≈690 at 1440, but at 390 the canvas starts at y≈1020.
evidence.craft: Tokens are on :root, CSS and JS are in separate files, and the total weight is about 66 KB with no web fonts loaded. But probe axe reports 17 serious color-contrast nodes (e.g. --ink-3 #8a8073 .tiny/.hero-note text on linen). There are 31 text elements under 12px: thread-strip codes and .pill at 10.9px, stats dt at 11.5px, and a 7px SVG label in step 2. At 320 the header 'Open the beta editor' (nowrap) overflows by 68px (scrollWidth 388). Dead code: .palette-empty and strokeStarted.
evidence.mobile: At 390 there is no overflow, but .site-nav is display:none under 760px with no menu button, so the Editor/How/Sellers/FAQ links are unreachable on a phone. The toolbar tools collapse to 36x36 icon-only buttons named only by title. The Width/Threads selects are 29px tall and the Grid checkbox label is 21px tall. The canvas is 312px, so cells are about 13px. Tapping the canvas at 390 works (count 309 to 308). The toast is fixed at the bottom, so feedback stays visible.
evidence.honesty: Clicking hero 'Open the beta editor' scrolls to the demo, and only then does a toast say 'The beta is moving to its permanent address. Until then, the editor below is the real thing.' The disclosure comes after the click and contradicts the FAQ ('The editor on this page uses a short sample of the range; the beta editor matches against the full catalogue'). The page also invents a mailto address and a retention policy for the unseen beta ('keeps your photo only as long as it takes'). Sample artwork is labelled ('Both sample patterns are drawn by us').
evidence.interaction: No console or page errors across the full run. Edge inputs: a .txt file gives the toast 'That file is not an image', a corrupt PNG gives 'Could not read that image', and a 10x1000 image is clamped to 40x80 (aspect silently distorted). One toast reads 'using 1 threads'. Changing the Width/Threads selects after an import does nothing until you re-upload, and re-picking the same file is a no-op. Escape does not close the open catalogue. The keyboard path works: arrows plus Enter stitch on the canvas, B/F/I/E switch tools, and Ctrl+Z undoes. The canvas has role=img, so edits are not announced to screen readers.
evidence.copy: Specific and from the stitcher's world ('Fix a blotchy cheek, swap a thread you don't have, drop the colour count before you buy floss'; 'the key you print is the shopping list'). Weakened by the CTA toast contradicting the FAQ, and by 'using 1 threads'.
evidence.first_screen: At 1440 the promise and CTA are visible and the editor toolbar just peeks in at the bottom, with the canvas below the fold. At 390 the first screen shows the H1, lede, CTA and 'Try it' chips but no pattern. The primary label promises a destination it doesn't reach.

problems: The primary action 'Open the beta editor' (header, hero and final) does not open a beta editor. It scrolls to the on-page demo, and the disclosure comes only in a post-click toast that contradicts the FAQ.
Below 760px there is no navigation at all (the nav is hidden, with no menu button). The page also has 17 axe contrast failures and 31 text nodes under 12px, down to 7px.
It invents a contact address (hello@crossling.app) and beta data-retention claims the brief did not supply. The header CTA overflows by 68px at 320.

hard_fail_flags.evidence: The most prominent first-screen action at 1440 is labelled 'Open the beta editor' (also in the header and the final section). It does not open any beta editor. app.js has CONFIG.BETA_URL='' and the click handler calls preventDefault() and scrolls the page to #editor, the on-page demo. That demo is, per the page's own FAQ, a reduced sample ('uses a short sample of the range… the beta editor matches against the full catalogue'). The only disclosure is a toast shown after the click. This matches the 'label names a destination it does not reach (… that scrolls the page)' case.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P004/A/index.html from disk at 1440x900. Click the red 'Open the beta editor' button in the hero. The URL is unchanged, the page scrolls to 'Try it: a pattern you can edit', and a toast reads 'The beta is moving to its permanent address…'. Compare with the FAQ answer 'Which threads does it use?'.

evidence.clarity: H1 'Turn a photo into a cross-stitch pattern, then change any stitch.' plus 'a pattern editor for cross-stitchers' and the CTA 'Try the sample editor', followed by 'It runs here in your browser on a sample picture.' What, who and next step are all in the first screen at 1440 and 390.
evidence.fit: It resolves the missing beta address deliberately: every CTA is 'Try the sample editor', and the final section says 'The full beta editor doesn't have its address yet; its link will sit here when it does.' The commercial-use tension is handled by a note ('isn't settled yet') and a Pricing row. Sellers get a paragraph and a note but no way to register interest. There is no own-photo import on the page; recolouring a small pattern is covered.
evidence.distinctiveness: The editor sits in the hero, and the source drawing, the 12/22/40-stitch size comparison and the step art are all generated from the same pear SDF and charting code. Square-cornered controls and a utilitarian grotesque. The section order (sizes, how, who, pricing, final CTA) is still conventional.
evidence.proof: Operated at 1440: Stitch (status 'Stitched row 1, column 1 in 433 Medium brown.'), drag, Unpick, Swap colour ('Swapped n stitches of … for …'), adding 801 from 'More threads', Chart view with symbols, Start over, and the 4/7/10 thread re-chart. The thread list and totals update live. The size captions are arithmetically right (40/14×2.54=7.3 cm; 40/18×2.54=5.6 cm). It is sample-only, with no own photo.
evidence.craft: The CSS has a token and spacing scale (--s1..--s6, --sec, --gutter). Probe axe finds 0 violations, the smallest text is 13px, and there is no overflow at dpr 1. But fit() sets the canvas backing size to css×devicePixelRatio and never sets a CSS width, and drawSource uses putImageData, which ignores the transform. At deviceScaleFactor 2 at 1440: the hero editor's source thumbnail fills only the top-left quarter of its 44px box; step 1 art draws the pear in a quarter of a 440px canvas that spills out of its card with the grid overrunning; and the step 3 canvases render at 308px. At 768 dpr2 the page overflows by 18px. The neutral dpr-1 screenshots hide all of this. Two inline style attributes.
evidence.mobile: At 390 (dpr 1): the Menu button (69x44) opens the nav with aria-expanded=true, Escape closes it and returns focus, and tapping a link closes it. The CTA is 48px tall, tool buttons are 40px and swatches 36px. Tapping the grid stitches. But the status line that gives feedback sits at y=1851 while the grid ends at y=1122, so feedback is off-screen. At 390x844 with deviceScaleFactor 3 (a real phone), scrollWidth is 539: the 'How it works' headings and body text run past the right edge (art-cut 660px, art-before/after 462px).
evidence.honesty: Labels sit where the example appears: 'Sample only: the source is a drawing, not a photo. The beta editor takes your own photos.', 'Counts come from this sample', and 'shades on screen are approximate'. The CTA says what happens before the click. No invented contact details. 'The beta is free to use' and 'nothing will be charged before that' go slightly beyond the brief.
evidence.interaction: Native radio fieldsets with legends drive tools, view, count and swatches, and arrow keys move between options. The canvas has role=application with an aria-describedby live status that announces every cell, including edge messages ('already bare fabric', 'That square is bare fabric; choose a stitched square…'). Undo and Start over work. Bug: choose 4 under 'Threads from the picture' and the status says 'Your edits were cleared; Undo brings them back.' Clicking Undo throws 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '2')' six times, blanks the canvas and leaves the thread list stale. History stores grid indices but not the threads array. 'Start over' recovers.
evidence.copy: Precise and well written: 'Each square of the grid takes the average colour of the picture under it, so fine lines get blurred. That is normal and it is why step three exists.' 'A stem, an eye, a whisker: averages lose small things.' Status microcopy is written rather than defaulted. The Undo hint promises something that crashes.
evidence.first_screen: At 1440 the promise, the CTA and the operable editor (grid, tools and thread list) are all in one viewport. At 390 the promise, CTA and the editor header with its sample label are visible, but the grid starts at about y≈800, so the artifact is just below the fold.

problems: The canvas fit() helper ignores devicePixelRatio for CSS size and putImageData. On every retina or phone screen the hero thumbnail renders as a quarter-size image and the step art breaks out of its cards. On a dpr-3 phone at 390 this causes 149px of sideways scroll with 'How it works' text cut off.
Changing the thread count and then pressing Undo (as the status line invites) throws TypeError and blanks the editor canvas.
At 390 the editor's status feedback renders about 730px below the grid, and sellers get no action beyond a note.

hard_fail_flags.evidence: At 390x844 with a phone's device pixel ratio, the 'How it works' section is wider than the viewport. With deviceScaleFactor 3, document scrollWidth is 539 against clientWidth 390. canvas#art-cut renders 660px wide and #art-before/#art-after 462px, because fit() sets canvas.width=css×dpr without a CSS width. The grid column grows with it, so the step h3 'Each square is matched to a thread you can buy' and the step paragraph ('…so fine lines get blurred…') are cut at the right edge and readable only by scrolling sideways. The same bug gives scrollWidth 429 at dpr 2.
hard_fail_flags.steps: In Playwright, use newContext({viewport:{width:390,height:844}, deviceScaleFactor:3, isMobile:true, hasTouch:true}) and open packets/P004/B/index.html from disk. Evaluate document.documentElement.scrollWidth (expect 539). Scroll to #how: the step text and the canvases run off the right edge. With deviceScaleFactor 1 (the operator probe) the bug does not appear.

reason: B has the sounder engineering base: an axe-clean page, no text under 13px, native radio controls with a live status for every edit, a working mobile menu, and a primary action that does exactly what its label says. Its two serious bugs (the DPR canvas sizing and history not storing the thread set) are each a few-line fix. A runs without errors and handles file edge cases well, but its primary action is mislabelled and it has no mobile navigation and 17 contrast failures. If the adjudicator confirms B's high-DPR overflow as HF3, or judges B's retina breakage worse than A's CTA, I would ship A instead.
